core_obligations: Define W as the union of the images of all morphisms into X which are flat and locally of finite presentation, syntomic, smooth or etale and whose composite with f has the property (proof lines 6902-6908).
Show that W is open, using that every such morphism is open (proof lines 6909-6911).
Show that the restriction of f to W has the property, by exhibiting the chosen morphisms over W as a covering in the relevant topology and applying locality on the source (proof lines 6911-6914).
Conclude maximality from the construction, and deduce the compatibility of W with pullback along a morphism of the allowed kind for the composite (proof lines 6914-6916).
proof_roadmap: Construct W as a union of images (proof lines 6902-6908).
The restriction to W has the property, by locality (proof lines 6911-6914).
Maximality and compatibility with base change on the source, from the construction (proof lines 6914-6916).
difficulty_reason: For a property of morphisms that is local on the source in one of the topologies fppf, syntomic, smooth or etale, the lemma produces for every morphism f : X to Y a largest open W(f) on which the restriction of f has the property, and asserts that pulling W back along a flat finitely presented, syntomic, smooth or etale morphism g : X' to X gives the corresponding open for the composite (statement lines 6889-6899). The proof constructs W as the union of the images of all morphisms into X of the allowed kind whose composite with f has the property; openness of those morphisms makes the union open (proof lines 6902-6911), and the substantive point is that the restriction of f to this union has the property, which follows because the chosen morphisms form a covering of the union in the relevant topology and the property is local on the source (proof lines 6911-6914). Maximality is then immediate from the construction, since every open on which the restriction of f has the property is itself one of the morphisms entering the union, and the compatibility assertion is likewise read off from the construction rather than recomputed (proof lines 6914-6916). The claim is H2: the argument is a genuine construction whose two properties, that the union has the property and that it is the largest such open, both have to be justified, the first through the locality hypothesis.
